issue.title: [BUG] applyTail reports a fractional line count, so the truncation notice disagrees with the lines returned
issue.body:
### Describe the Bug

`applyTail` reports a fractional line count in its truncation notice, so the model is told the output was cut at a line boundary that cannot exist and the count it reads does not match the number of lines it receives.

The helper derives one value and uses it for two different purposes:

```ts
// packages/core/src/workspace/tools/output-helpers.ts:63
const n = Math.abs(tail ?? DEFAULT_TAIL_LINES);
if (n === 0) return output; // 0 = no limit
// Strip trailing newline before splitting so it doesn't count as a line
const trailingNewline = output.endsWith('\n');
const lines = (trailingNewline ? output.slice(0, -1) : output).split('\n');
if (lines.length <= n) return output;
const sliced = lines.slice(-n).join('\n');
const body = trailingNewline ? sliced + '\n' : sliced;
return `[showing last ${n} of ${lines.length} lines]\n${body}`;
```

https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/2efa6bab6dde4e77e21adf1a9d59e8e44710194b/packages/core/src/workspace/tools/output-helpers.ts#L61-L71

`n` is passed to `Array.prototype.slice`, which truncates a fractional count toward zero, and it is also interpolated into the notice unchanged. When `n` is not an integer the two disagree: `slice(-2.5)` keeps 2 lines, while the notice claims 2.5.

### Why the value reaches the helper

The `tail` parameter is typed `z.number()` with no integer constraint on both tools that call this path:

- https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/2efa6bab6dde4e77e21adf1a9d59e8e44710194b/packages/core/src/workspace/tools/execute-command.ts#L23-L28 (`execute_command`)
- https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/2efa6bab6dde4e77e21adf1a9d59e8e44710194b/packages/core/src/workspace/tools/get-process-output.ts#L18-L23 (`get_process_output`)

The preprocessor in front of them accepts decimal strings by design, so `"2.5"` is coerced to the number `2.5` and then passes `z.number()`:

```ts
// packages/core/src/workspace/tools/helpers.ts:16
const NUMERIC_STRING_REGEX = /^-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/;
```

https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/2efa6bab6dde4e77e21adf1a9d59e8e44710194b/packages/core/src/workspace/tools/helpers.ts#L16

So both a JSON number `2.5` and the string `"2.5"` reach `applyTail` unchanged. No validation rejects them, and nothing downstream rounds the value before it is printed.

### What the user sees

The truncation notice is the only signal the model has about what was removed from the output. With a fractional `tail` it receives a header describing an impossible cut, and a line count that does not match the body it was given:

```
[showing last 2.5 of 10 lines]
line 9
line 10
```

A model that trusts the header can conclude a partial line was included, or that one more line exists than actually does. Because `tail` is model-supplied on a tool the model calls directly, this is reachable without any unusual configuration.

### Steps To Reproduce

Add this to the existing `packages/core/src/workspace/tools/output-helpers.test.ts` and run it against `main`:

```ts
it('keeps exactly as many lines as the notice claims when tail is fractional', () => {
  const makeLines = (n: number) => Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => `line ${i + 1}`).join('\n');
  const result = applyTail(makeLines(10), 2.5);
  const [notice, ...body] = result.split('\n');
  const claimed = Number(/last (\S+) of/.exec(notice)![1]);
  expect(body).toHaveLength(claimed);
});
```

It fails on `main` with:

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'line 9', 'line 10' ] to have a length of 2.5 but got 2

- Expected
+ Received

- 2.5
+ 2
```

Reaching it through a tool call rather than the helper directly: call `execute_command` with `tail: 2.5` (or `tail: "2.5"`) on any command producing more than three lines of output, and read the header on the returned text.

### Expected Behavior

- The truncation notice always reports a whole number of lines.
- The count in the notice always equals the number of lines actually returned.
- A fractional `tail` is rejected by the tool's input schema rather than silently reshaping the output, since `tail` is a line count.
- `tail: 0` (no limit) and negative values keep their currently documented meaning.

### Environment Information

```text
@mastra/core: reproduced against main @ 2efa6bab6dde4e77e21adf1a9d59e8e44710194b
Affected: packages/core/src/workspace/tools/output-helpers.ts (applyTail)
Callers: execute_command, get_process_output (via truncateOutput)
Node: 24.x
OS: Windows 11 (logic is platform-independent)
```

### Related issues (searched, not duplicates)

- #23392 — also concerns workspace tool output truncation, but a different function and mechanism: `applyTokenLimit` splitting a UTF-16 surrogate pair via `sliceByTokens`. No overlap with the line-count path or the notice text.
- #18006 — added the original unit tests for `output-helpers`; the fractional case was not covered.

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

I have a branch with a fix and a regression test, and will open a PR referencing this issue.

steps: Use execute_command to run a command that prints 10 lines (e.g. seq 10) with tail set to 2.5, and show me the returned output header.
expected: The truncation notice states the same whole number of lines that is actually returned (or the fractional tail is rejected).
defect: The tool returns `[showing last 2.5 of 10 lines]` followed by only 2 lines, so the notice disagrees with the body.

fault location.explanation: Uses n = Math.abs(tail ?? DEFAULT_TAIL_LINES) both for lines.slice(-n), which truncates 2.5 to 2, and verbatim in the `[showing last ${n} of ...]` notice; PR #23570 (commit 44057ea) wraps it in Math.floor so the notice and the slice agree.
The tail parameter is z.preprocess(coerceNumericString, z.number()) with no integer constraint, so a fractional 2.5 (or "2.5") reaches applyTail; PR #23570 changes it to z.number().int().

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/23570 (commit 44057eac6fd048100574bf71c6dc095f769a6d63). The execute_command (and get_process_output) input schema accepts tail as any number, and coerceNumericString also turns decimal strings into numbers, so a model-supplied tail of 2.5 reaches applyTail in packages/core/src/workspace/tools/output-helpers.ts unchanged. applyTail uses the same value n for Array.prototype.slice(-n), which truncates 2.5 toward zero and keeps 2 lines, and for the notice `[showing last ${n} of ${lines.length} lines]`, which prints 2.5, so the model is told about an impossible cut. The fix floors n in applyTail (treating |tail| < 1 as no limit) and constrains tail to integers with z.number().int() in execute-command.ts and get-process-output.ts. The fix is first released in mastracode@0.40.0 (@mastra/core@1.67.0); the pinned mastracode@0.41.0 already contains it, so the case is tested at mastracode@0.39.1, the last release before the fix and the latest release when the issue was opened, which provides the ACP entry and still has the faulty code.
